3. The petitioner's case in Writ Petition No. 207/86 is that they purchased the land in question from one Siddique Ahmed by a registered kabala dated 15.8.79. Originally the land was recorded in the name of its owner Abdur Rahman in RS khatian. Subsequently Fazar Rahman, the heir of Abdur Rahman, sold the same to one Nur Mohammad by registered deed of sale and Nur Mohammad sold the same in favour of one Siddique Ahmed by a registered kabala dated 3.12.69. The present petitioners purchased the suit land from the said Siddique Ahmed. The petitioners claim that the suit land be recorded in their names. That one Mohammad Harunur Rashid filed an objection under section 19(1) of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in objection Case No. 139 dated 15.10.1980 objecting the entry of the name of the respondent No.2 in the draft record of rights. The objection was not allowed. 

 6. In Writ Petition No. 208 of 1986 the case of the petitioner Mosammat Sabera Begum is that one Bujarat was instituted by the respondent Nos. 2-3 impleading the petitioner as the second party before the Revenue Authority. The case was disposed of ex parte by order dated 23.6.77 wherein the name of the petitioner in the khatian was directed to be struck off and those of respondent Nos. 2-5 were to be recorded. Against the said order the petitioner filed objection case impleading the respondent Nos. 2-5 as opposite parties. The Revenue Officer considered the objection and disposed of the case by his order dated 31.5.79 maintaining the order recording the name of the respondents passed in the Biujarat dispute case. It is the case of the petitioner that the original owner of the case land was one Abdur Rahman and his name appeared in the RS khatian in Korfa right The said RS khatian was under khatian No. 25 of Jote No. 1 and the owner of the said jote No. 1 was one Abdul Aziz Sarang in raiyati right. The said Jotedar having defaulted in payment of revenue, the Jote was put to auction and ultimately the entire lands vested in the Government. One Abdus Salam prayed for re-settlement of the case land and his prayer was allowed and accordingly he became tenant directly under the Government Abdus Salam also defaulted in payment of rent and a Certificate case was started being Certificate Case No. 357 of 1945-46. The land in question was auction sold to one Ahmedur Rahman on 16.7.1946 and the sale was confirmed on 16.9.1946 and possession was delivered on 18.1.1948. The said Ahmedur Rahman got his name mutated in the RS khatian. The said auction purchaser while in possession sold the land to the petitioner by a registered kabala being kabala No. 4245 dated 21.6.1960 and since then she has been in possession of the case lands. The petitioner's name has been duly recorded in the SA khatian which has been finally published. The petitioner's name was also correctly recorded in the present khatian as per his title and possession. After the Field Survey the present respondent Nos. 5 filed a dispute case and managed to get their names recorded by suppressing notices. 

 7. The case of the respondent that the land originally belonged to one Abdur Rahman to the extent of 16 annas share and RS khatian No. 30/1 has been finally published in the name of the said Abdur Rahman. On his death, the respondent Nos. 2-5 were in possession of the case land as his heirs. That while in such possession they sold the land in favour of Jalalabad Housing Society and delivered possession to the said Society. As against the order the petitioner filed an appeal to the Revenue Authority and the case was registered as Appeal Case No. 23994/80. The Appellate Authority by its order dated 16.9.84 allowed the appeal and directed the recording of the name of the petitioner in the khatian by striking out the names of the respondents. Thereafter the respondent Nos. 2-5 filed a Review petition on 14.10.84 before the said appellate authority and the appellate authority heard the matter and considered the case rejecting the Review petition and maintained his earlier decision by order dated 16.9.84. That thereafter the respondent Nos. 2-5 filed a second appellation for review of the order dated 16.9.84 before the Director of Land Records. The Director of Land Records by the impugned order dated 31.3.86 allowed the second review petition of the respondents by setting aside the order dated 16.9.84 passed by the appellate authority.
